title: Artificial Intelligence and Public Standards: government response to report
description: The government's response to the Committee's 2020 report Artificial Intelligence and Public Standards
summary: The UK government has released its response to the 2020 Committee report on Artificial Intelligence and Public Standards, outlining measures to strengthen AI governance, promote transparency, and ensure ethical use across public services. It commits to developing clear standards, encouraging industry collaboration, and supporting research to address societal risks associated with AI deployment.

title: ​​Ofqual’s approach to regulating the use of artificial intelligence in the qualifications sector​
description: Published in response to a request from the Secretary of State for Education, the Secretary of State for Science, Innovation and Technology, and the Secretary of State for Business and Trade.
summary: Ofqual has released a policy to guide how artificial intelligence can be used in the qualifications sector, outlining rules and safeguards to protect exam integrity and fairness. The document was issued in response to a joint request from the Secretaries of State for Education, Science, Innovation and Technology, and Business and Trade.

title: Report and impact assessment on Copyright and Artificial Intelligence
description: A report and impact assessment on the use of copyright works in the development of artificial intelligence (AI) systems.
summary: This report examines how copyright laws affect the development of AI, including how copyrighted content is used for training and potential legal challenges. It assesses the broader impact on creators, developers, and the AI industry, offering recommendations for balancing innovation with intellectual property protection.

title: Government response to the House of Lords Select Committee on Artificial Intelligence
description: Government response to the Lords Select Committee on Artificial Intelligence report ‘AI in the UK: No Room for Complacency’.
summary: The UK government has issued a response to the House of Lords Select Committee’s report “AI in the UK: No Room for Complacency,” outlining its commitments to harness AI’s benefits while addressing risks. It highlights plans for investment, regulation, and workforce support to ensure AI development remains safe, fair, and economically productive.

title: AI and Public Standards – Terms of Reference
description: Terms of Reference and FAQs for the Committee's review into artificial intelligence and public standards.
summary: This document lays out the purpose, scope, and duties of a committee that will study how artificial intelligence should be governed in public settings. It also contains a FAQ section explaining the committee’s work, its main focus areas, and how it will carry out its review.

title: CSPL submission to Science and Technology Committee inquiry on Governance of AI
description: CSPL has submitted written evidence to the Science and Technology Committee's inquiry on Governance of Artificial Intelligence.
summary: CSPL has submitted written evidence to the Science and Technology Committee’s inquiry on the governance of artificial intelligence, presenting its views on policy and regulatory matters. The submission aims to inform the committee’s work and help shape national AI governance frameworks.

title: Impact of AI on the regulation of medical products
description: Implementing the Artificial Intelligence (AI) White Paper principles.
summary: The document discusses how artificial intelligence affects the regulation of medical products, highlighting the need for updated guidelines and oversight. It focuses on implementing the AI White Paper principles to ensure safety, transparency, and ethical use in medical product development and approval.

title: Defence Artificial Intelligence Strategy
description: Our vision is that, in terms of AI, we will be the world’s most effective, efficient, trusted and influential Defence organisation for our size.
summary: The Defence Artificial Intelligence Strategy aims to make our military the most effective, efficient, trusted, and influential AI-powered organization in the world, relative to our size. This vision focuses on leveraging AI to enhance defence capabilities and maintain a leading position in global security.

title: Transport artificial intelligence action plan
description: Sets out how DfT will work with the transport sector to exploit the opportunities from AI while managing potential risks.
summary: The Transport Artificial Intelligence Action Plan explains how the Department for Transport will partner with transport companies to use AI technologies to improve efficiency, safety, and passenger experience. It also outlines measures to mitigate risks such as privacy, security, and ethical concerns, ensuring AI deployment is safe, transparent, and benefits all stakeholders.

title: Copyright and artificial intelligence: progress report
description: A progress report on the use of copyright works in the development of AI systems, under Section 137 of the Data (Use and Access) Act.
summary: This report examines how copyrighted works are used to train and develop AI systems, focusing on compliance with Section 137 of the Data (Use and Access) Act. It outlines current practices, challenges, and recommendations for balancing innovation and copyright protection.
